source: Epic Fight 20.14.17: assets/epicfight/animmodels/animations/biped/living/<pose>.json joint keyframes composed on the stock biped armature (biped.json) with efanim (JsonAssetLoader's Blender->Minecraft root rotation Rx(-90)); the item frame is pose[Tool_R] * T(0,0,-0.13) * Rx(-90) (RenderItemBase.GLOBAL_MAINHAND_ITEM_TRANSFORMS for Tool_R). Averaged over one animation loop (64 samples); the hand frame turns by at most `max_rotation_deviation_deg` degrees away from the mean during the loop. Regenerate with holdpose.derive_frames() (needs the Epic Fight jar). Cross-checked against a dev client: Epic Fight's own pose matrix of Tool_R while the Nightingale boss idles (hold_spear) has origin (0.250, 0.826, 0.415) and the same axes to 3 decimals.
space: wielder body space at entity scale 1: x = wielder's right, y = up, z = backwards (the wielder faces -z), units = blocks (the stock biped is 1.8 tall)
item_frame: axes[0], axes[1], axes[2] are the item model's local x (sprite right), y (sprite up) and z (sprite normal) directions in body space after Epic Fight's hand correction; origin is where the item model's pivot (the display transform origin) sits
